openings.claim: Certificate-driven paired review could support reproducible further-evaluation decisions despite selective label unavailability. Separate acquisition ranking from certification: in a spreadsheet/local script, bound flagged-row candidate-minus-baseline correctness gains and total/slice intervals. Inspect threshold-relevant rows in the slice at the loss boundary first, then total-gain-relevant rows; break ties by record identifier. Recompute after each returned label; remove unavailable rows from acquisition while retaining their uncertainty.
openings.discriminator: Versus balanced slice-quota inspection with identifier ordering, boundary-first review may support decisions with fewer adjudications. Compare certified decisions, remaining interval widths, labels consumed and elapsed time. Equal efficiency, more unresolved outcomes, or disagreement with the full-label key defeats the advantage.
openings.probe: Use only supplied records/labels. Run both policies on matched copies with independently reset sixteen-label allowances and seventy-minute limits; withhold four preselected rows. Log every selection, returned label, unavailable attempt and time. Advance only if total lower gain >=4 and every slice lower gain >=-2. Reject only if total upper gain <4 or some slice upper gain <-2. Otherwise report unresolved, including inconclusive interval combinations. Freeze decisions, affected-slice summaries and logs before opening the full-label key. Compare support and resource use; this probes review policy, not deployment readiness.
openings.uncertainty: Flag identification and supplied label vocabulary must permit bounds covering every permissible completion; missing information forces unresolved, and coarse bounds may remain inconclusive. Accessible pivotal rows and affordable interval computation are necessary but unestablished. Unavailable attempts consume no adjudication allowance, but time/logging still matter. A cap alone does not establish informative feasibility.

lineage.reason: Retains causal separation, acquisition ordering, conservative certificates, complete rival/defeat comparison, resource limits and uncertainties.

decision: Retain one uncertain policy hypothesis for bounded comparison; supplied provisional observations establish neither comparative advantage nor an advance/reject certificate.
